title: Rows columns and schemas
goals: Check types and units as well as names

prerequisite.answer: Look up the value associated with the key "used" in that record.

vocabulary: Rules for the fields and values in records
A category such as integer or text
The quantity scale attached to a number
A rule a valid record must satisfy

blocks.text: A fictional classroom logs the duration of each activity. Before comparing durations, define a schema: activity is nonempty text, minutes is an integer from 0 through 60, and each row describes one activity session. These decisions make data interpretable.

blocks.title: Python 3 code
blocks.text:
rows = [{"activity": "Reading", "minutes": 12},
        {"activity": "Sorting", "minutes": 0}]
for row in rows:
    valid = (type(row["activity"]) is str
             and len(row["activity"]) > 0
             and type(row["minutes"]) is int
             and 0 <= row["minutes"] <= 60)
    print(valid)

blocks.title: Follow the evidence
blocks.caption: Read each row from left to right and connect the evidence to the stated rule.

blocks.text: The worked script prints True twice. type(value) is int checks the exact type here and avoids accepting a Boolean as a count. The chained comparison checks both boundaries. The example assumes both keys exist; next week handles missing fields. A zero duration is allowed by this written schema.

blocks.label: Would minutes of 61, "12" and 12 each pass? Explain the type distinction.

blocks.text: If one row records 120 seconds in the minutes field, a simple numeric total becomes misleading. Correct the source or explicitly convert and document it; renaming a column alone does not convert values.

A row can satisfy every schema rule and still be a wrong observation. Schema validation checks our stated structure and constraints, not whether someone measured honestly or selected a representative sample.

blocks.label: A row says Reading, 12 and passes. Does that establish the session really lasted 12 minutes?

workbook.title: State a schema
workbook.prompt: List the required fields, types and duration boundaries for the worked table.
workbook.answer: activity: nonempty text; minutes: integer from 0 to 60 inclusive.

workbook.title: Classify records
workbook.prompt: Classify minutes values 0, 60, -1 and 61 under this schema.

workbook.title: Repair a unit problem
workbook.prompt: A source says 180 seconds but the row says minutes: 180. Give a documented correction.
workbook.answer: Divide by 60 to record 3 minutes and retain the source value and conversion note.

workbook.title: Design a schema independently
workbook.prompt: For a fictional shelf audit, define label and book_count fields. Require a nonempty text label and an integer count from 0 to 40. Give two valid and two invalid records with reasons.
workbook.answer: Examples: A/0 and B/40 valid; empty label/5 invalid label; C/41 invalid range. Text "5" also fails the count type. Accept alternatives meeting the written rules.

workbook.title: Separate validity and truth
workbook.prompt: A row says Reading, 12 and passes. Does that establish the session really lasted 12 minutes?
workbook.answer: No. The value has a permitted structure but still needs trustworthy collection evidence.
